label: dense near-always-on feature (every step except often t=0); peaks when copying runs of g
explanation: Fires on about 90% of all steps (97% of steps after t=0) in every sequence, across all phases, tokens and lengths, with lift of roughly 1.0x on every variable. It is weakest at t=0 (rate 0.37) and t=1 (0.79). Activation rises slowly through the original phase and stays high through the delimiter and copy phases (copy rate 0.965). The predicate t>=1 gets F1 0.96 on dev only because the feature is dense. It contains no token-level structure. The largest activations all occur in the copy phase around outputs of the letter g, especially repeated g runs (input token before g, or g, with g being output). Even so, g-related steps cover only about 15% of the top activation quartile, so token identity explains only a small part of the magnitude. It does not respond selectively to any particular input token, digit or position beyond this.
